# Tasks: Daily Admin Report

**Input**: Design documents from `/specs/003-daily-admin-report/`

**Prerequisites**: plan.md (required), spec.md (required for user stories), research.md, data-model.md, contracts/

**Tests**: In this project (MacroGest Core), tests are MANDATORY: they validate real business rules with concrete data (Constitution Pr. V) and are generated by `@blendverse-tester` after implementation. Do not plan test tasks.

**Organization**: Tasks are grouped by user story to enable independent implementation and testing of each story.

## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description`

- **[P]**: Can run in parallel (different files, no dependencies)
- **[Story]**: Which user story this task belongs to (e.g., US1, US2, US3)
- Include exact file paths in descriptions

## Path Conventions

- **Backend**: `packages/server/src/`
- **Domains**: `packages/server/src/domains/[Domain]/`

**Independent Test**: Start the server, wait for the scheduler trigger (or execute manually), and confirm that an email is generated and sent to administrators of each active company. Validate without all content sections implemented — a basic template with placeholder data is sufficient.

## Dependencies & Execution Order

### Phase Dependencies

- **Setup (Phase 1)**: No dependencies - can start immediately
- **Foundational (Phase 2)**: Depends on Setup completion - BLOCKS all user stories
- **User Story 1 (Phase 3)**: Depends on Foundational - MVP (scheduler + basic email with stub orchestrator)
- **User Stories 2-5 (Phases 4-7)**: Depend on Foundational + User Story 1 - can run in parallel after US1
- **User Stories 6-8 (Phases 8-10)**: Depend on Foundational + User Story 1 - can run in parallel after US1
- **User Story 9 (Phase 11)**: Depends on User Story 1 - enhances error handling
- **Polish (Phase 12)**: Depends on all desired user stories being complete

### User Story Dependencies

- **User Story 1 (P1)**: Can start after Foundational (Phase 2) - No dependencies on other stories - **MVP** (uses stub orchestrator)
- **User Story 2 (P2)**: Can start after US1 - Adds Section 1 (employees on leave today)
- **User Story 3 (P2)**: Can start after US1 - Adds Section 2 (pending licenses)
- **User Story 4 (P2)**: Can start after US1 - Adds Section 3 (unsigned documents)
- **User Story 5 (P2)**: Can start after US1 - Adds Section 4 (pending disclaimer acceptances)
- **User Story 6 (P3)**: Can start after US1 - Adds Section 5 (upcoming vacations)
- **User Story 7 (P3)**: Can start after US1 - Adds Section 6 (expiring licenses)
- **User Story 8 (P3)**: Can start after US1 - Adds Section 7 (statistical summary) + **replaces stub with full orchestrator**
- **User Story 9 (P2)**: Can start after US1 - Enhances error handling and logging

### Within Each User Story

- Repository interface methods before implementation
- Implementation before use case
- Use case before template update
- Story complete before moving to next priority

### Parallel Opportunities

- All Setup tasks marked [P] can run in parallel
- All Foundational tasks marked [P] can run in parallel (within Phase 2)
- Once Foundational phase completes, User Story 1 must be done first (MVP)
- After US1, User Stories 2-8 can all run in parallel (if team capacity allows)
- User Story 9 can run in parallel with US2-US8
- Repository methods within a story marked [P] can run in parallel
- Different user stories can be worked on in parallel by different team members

## Implementation Strategy

### MVP First (User Story 1 Only)

1. Complete Phase 1: Setup
2. Complete Phase 2: Foundational (CRITICAL - blocks all stories)
3. Complete Phase 3: User Story 1 (scheduler + basic email with stub orchestrator + manual trigger)
4. **STOP and VALIDATE**: Test User Story 1 independently (scheduler runs, email sends with placeholder content)
5. Deploy/demo if ready — you have a working daily report system with placeholder content

### Incremental Delivery

1. Complete Setup + Foundational → Foundation ready
2. Add User Story 1 → Test independently → Deploy/Demo (MVP! with stub orchestrator)
3. Add User Stories 2-5 (P2 sections) → Test independently → Deploy/Demo
4. Add User Stories 6-8 (P3 sections) → Test independently → Deploy/Demo
5. **US8 includes replacing stub with full orchestrator** → Now all 7 sections are real
6. Add User Story 9 (resilience) → Test independently → Deploy/Demo
7. Each story adds value without breaking previous stories

### Parallel Team Strategy

With multiple developers:

1. Team completes Setup + Foundational together
2. Once Foundational is done, one developer implements User Story 1 (MVP with stub)
3. After US1 is complete:
   - Developer A: User Stories 2-5 (P2 sections)
   - Developer B: User Stories 6-8 (P3 sections, including full orchestrator in US8)
   - Developer C: User Story 9 (resilience)
4. Stories complete and integrate independently

---

## Notes

- [P] tasks = different files, no dependencies
- [Story] label maps task to specific user story for traceability
- Each user story should be independently completable and testable
- Commit after each task or logical group
- Stop at any checkpoint to validate story independently
- Avoid: vague tasks, same file conflicts, cross-story dependencies that break independence
- All repository methods must filter by `ownerId` from `RequestContext` (Constitution Pr. II)
- All use cases must be injected via Awilix DI (Constitution Pr. VII)
- No `any` types allowed (Constitution Pr. III)
- Barrel exports must follow hexagonal architecture rules (Constitution Pr. I)
- **GenerateDailyReportStub** is used in US1 to allow MVP delivery before section use cases exist
- **GenerateDailyReport** (full orchestrator) replaces the stub in US8 after all 7 section use cases are implemented
- **DailyReportEmailSender** port/adapter pattern ensures hexagonal architecture compliance (use cases don't depend on infrastructure)
